t: Real Research Today: Brain Maintenance Programs
title: Real Research Today: Brain Maintenance Programs
definition: Today's documented research behind Brain Maintenance Programs.
description:
The road to Brain Maintenance Programs is already being paved. David Sinclair's Harvard lab demonstrated age reversal in mice via partial cellular reprogramming. The UK Biobank and All of Us programs gather million-person health datasets for longevity research.

The WHO's ICD-11 added an extension code for aging-related conditions, legitimizing the field. Together these programs form the assessment labs foundation that Brain Maintenance Programs will build on — the program logistics results, the lifestyle medicine methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as program logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Brain Maintenance Programs Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Brain Maintenance Programs: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Brain Maintenance Programs — long-term programs keeping aging brains sharp.

Phase 1 — Prove (assessment labs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (program logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (lifestyle medicine): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (cognitive reserve): program hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and neurology-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
